A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Equivariant Neural Tangent Kernels by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original Monte Carlo kernel-convergence experiments and histological-image classification results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report kernel convergence, histological-image classification, QM9 molecular-energy regression, and MNIST/CIFAR10 ensemble experiments.

M1.justification: Beyond the retained general recursions and planar implementation, v2 adds Fourier-domain SO(3) kernel computation and a molecular pipeline using spherical per-atom inputs and aggregation (Section 4.3, Appendix D, Table 2). Fourier computation was future work in v1. The main pooling definition also changes from inverse-square-root-volume normalization to inverse-volume normalization, although Appendix C retains the earlier convention.

E1.justification: v1's empirical application coverage is histological-image classification. v2 adds QM9 molecular-energy regression and MNIST/CIFAR10 training with artificial out-of-distribution inputs for ensemble comparisons. This substantially expands tasks, domains, and test conditions, including continuous 3D rotational symmetry.

E2.justification: The CNN-kernel comparator for histology is retained. v2 additionally evaluates an MLP-kernel comparator against the SO(3) molecular predictor and data-augmented finite-width CNN ensembles against GCNN ensembles (Figures 2, 4, and 6). These introduce substantive comparison methods beyond extending the original comparator pair to another dataset.

E3.justification: The histology training-set range expands from 200 to 1000 images. Added protocols include QM9 energy prediction evaluated by MAE and 20-epoch comparisons of out-of-distribution logit distances across ensemble sizes 1, 3, 8, and 100. Table 2 specifies different nonlinearities for the new molecular comparison: ReLU for the MLP and Erf for the GCNN.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses testing whether augmentation-equivalence persists at finite width, varying ensemble size and tracking prediction discrepancies throughout training on out-of-distribution inputs (Figures 2 and 6, Appendix F.4). These address a new robustness and sensitivity question. The original width-convergence analysis remains, with its NNGP panel relocated.

E5.justification: The retained kernel-convergence experiment still averages 1000 initializations and reports bands of one standard deviation. The new application and ensemble-comparison plots introduce no confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Ensemble size is varied as an experimental configuration rather than reported as repeated evaluation trials.

E6.justification: v2 adds molecular-energy results favoring the SO(3) kernel over the MLP and ensemble results showing generally smaller prediction discrepancies for larger ensembles. The expanded histology curve reports approximately 74% GCNN versus 57% CNN accuracy at 1000 training images, beyond v1's 200-image range. These are additional results, not evidence of a same-setting improvement over v1; the kernel-convergence findings are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorems 5–7 and Appendix E proofs connecting full augmentation, group-averaged kernels, and GCNN ensemble means, plus SO(3) Fourier-recursion lemmas and proofs in Appendix D. It also makes kernel right-invariance conditional on invariant filter supports, whereas v1's Remark 2 stated it unconditionally. Existing group and planar recursions are largely retained or relocated.

C1.justification: The original contribution of deriving equivariant kernel recursions remains. v2 adds a central claim about matching augmentation-based and equivariant mean training predictions at infinite width, including off-manifold inputs, with approximate finite-width evidence. Its claimed practical contributions also expand from planar medical-image prediction to SO(3) kernels and molecular-energy prediction.

C2.justification: v2 develops substantive interpretations of augmentation-equivalence, explicitly distinguishing equal ensemble means from unequal distributions of individual networks (Section 5.4). It states quadratic-loss and infinite-width conditions, with the augmentation proof restricted to finite groups, and explains the SO(3) implementation's global-filter restriction. These substantially expand applicability boundaries beyond v1's general research outlook.

D1.justification: Appendix F and Tables 1–3 add extensive reproducibility information: histology filter sizes and a 1000-image test set, molecular features, grids, bandlimits, smoothing parameter and a 100-molecule test set, and finite-width ensemble architectures. s2fft and escnn are newly identified dependencies. Details newly disclosed for the retained histology experiment do not establish that those settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 reframes the motivation around the equivariance-versus-augmentation debate, introducing AlphaFold 3, Does equivariance matter at scale?, and Swallowing the Bitter Pill. It adds spherical-computation and ensemble-equivariance literature while removing several references supporting v1's future-work discussion. This materially changes research positioning beyond bibliography maintenance.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around augmentation-equivalence. Background material is condensed or moved to Appendix A, planar formulas and proofs are consolidated in Appendix C, and the CNN warm-up derivation is removed. A new central theory section replaces much of the earlier narrative emphasis, and the extended research outlook becomes a short conclusion.

P2.justification: v1's paired convergence panels become separate v2 Figures 1 and 5, and the medical learning curve is redrawn with an expanded axis. v2 adds molecular and ensemble-comparison plots, out-of-distribution example images, and three architecture tables. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The augmentation-equivalence results give the kernel framework a substantive explanatory application that v1 lacked, supported by finite-width checks. The SO(3) construction also realizes Fourier computation left as future work in v1, while Appendix F substantially improves experimental documentation. Different QM9 nonlinearities complicate attribution, and the pooling conventions are not fully reconciled between the main text and Appendix C, but these issues do not outweigh the substantial theoretical and practical gains.
